messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: readCdfGroupNames
parts:
Hi,

I had a question about readCdfGroupNames(). There is a logical option
'truncateGroupNames' which the help says indicates 'whether unit names
should be stripped from the beginning of group names'. This makes it
sound like otherwise, the unit name is pasted to EVERY group name in
some way.

But in practice, I think this seems to operate only if the group name
matches the unit name and otherwise have no effect. In the case that the
group name matches the unit name, if option is T, it returns "" as the
group name and if F it returns the group name (which is same as the unit
name). This is indeed what I want, but I want to check that I am not
incorrect.

Thanks,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] readCdfGroupNames
parts:
Hi.

Ok, this is an affxparser specific question, so in future please post
those to the Bioconductor list.

On 11/12/2007, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
>
> I had a question about readCdfGroupNames(). There is a logical option
> 'truncateGroupNames' which the help says indicates 'whether unit names
> should be stripped from the beginning of group names'. This makes it
> sound like otherwise, the unit name is pasted to EVERY group name in
> some way.
>
> But in practice, I think this seems to operate only if the group name
> matches the unit name and otherwise have no effect. In the case that the
> group name matches the unit name, if option is T, it returns "" as the
> group name and if F it returns the group name (which is same as the unit
> name). This is indeed what I want, but I want to check that I am not
> incorrect.

Yes, if the unit name is a prefix of a group name, and
truncateGroupNames=TRUE (default), then that prefix is excluded. For
example, if unit name is 'SNP_A-0923020' and the group name is
'SNP_A-0923020A', then the returned group name is 'A' if
truncateGroupNames=TRUE, and 'SNP_A-0923020A' if
truncateGroupNames=FALSE.

If I recall it correctly, the reason for adding this in the first
place was that for the same public SNP data stored as binary and as
ASCII would return different group names. In the binary format, the
group names where simply 'A', 'C', 'G', or 'T' (indicating the
allele), whereas when stored in ASCII format the group names had the
unit name appended. By making truncateGroupNames=TRUE by default the
user had one less thing to worry about. I looked at the logs, and Ken
added this argument to the affxparser v1.7.5, because before it was
hardwired to TRUE, cf.

Version: 1.7.5 [2007-03-08]
o Added argument 'truncateGroupNames' to readCdfGroupNames()
which defaults to TRUE for backward compatibility. When
TRUE, any prefix of group names identical to the unit name
will be stripped of the group names.

So, it looks like you're walking down the same exon-array path as him.

Speaking of it, I think we "forgot" to provide the same feature for
readCdfUnits(), so you probably have spotted an inconsistency.

/Henrik

>
> Thanks,
> Elizabeth
>
>
>
> >

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: readCdfGroupNames
parts:
Thanks Henrik and sorry about the posting; I'll continue the thread
here, but in the future I'll switch over. I always forget to check
which is from which package because they are so connected in my head.

I remembered that Ken was dealing with this, so I wanted to double
check. In the exon case (with Affy's definitions of units), if there
is a single group within a unit, the unit and group have the same
name. Otherwise, the unit names and the group names should be unique
(something I like to check...). Given this uniqueness, the truncate
option being set to F should give all the group names -- but for
truncate =T, then those groups get the names "". Regardless, the
function should never should give any more than the full group name or
some truncated version of it.

For some reason Ken never set the truncate option to F, but worked
with the blank string names which made the code clunky. So I'm trying
to figure out if there is a pitfall to just using this option...

Best,
Elizabeth
